title: The plan composer keeps its own sealed plan: derive it from the daemon's live plan

body:
## Summary
The Plan options composer shows the sealed plan and the chosen options from a module-level in-memory store, while the daemon persists the same plan and serves it as `plan.current`. Reload the console and the page forgets the live plan, offers 'Seal this plan' over an empty selection, and one click re-runs the planner LLM and replaces what Malakor will receive. Make the daemon's live plan the authority and derive the composer's state from it.

## Description
Today `session.ts` keeps `chosen` and `sealed` per report (session.ts:18-20) and PlanPage reads only those (PlanPage.tsx:38,46). The daemon writes `next_plan.json` on every choose (lib.rs:558-560) and serves it (rpc.rs:257-260); the contract plan carries `report_id` and `option_ids` (types.ts:2175-2180). The console keeps a second, volatile copy of daemon state, and the copy is the one the operator acts on.

The move leans on client-state `invalidation-strategy` (the server is the authority, the client learns by refetch) and `status-fsms` (name the states the flags combine into), and hitl-approval `resume-after-decision` (what the operator approves must be what is shown). A pure `planState.ts` derives `composerState(live, reportId, draft)` into named states - `none`, `live-here` (same | differs, with added/removed), `live-elsewhere` (sealed from another report), `unknown` (read failed). PlanPage reads `plan.current`, seeds the draft from `live.option_ids` when the live plan answers this report and the operator has not touched the selection, and labels the action by state: disabled 'This is the live plan', 'Replace the live plan' with the diff, or 'Seal this plan'. `sealed` and `seal` leave the session store; only the unsent draft (`chosen`) stays, which is the half-made choice the store's header says it exists for.

## Flow
- Plan tab mounts -> plan.proposals and plan.current in parallel
- composerState(live, reportId, draft) -> none / live-here(same|differs) / live-elsewhere / unknown
- draft untouched and live-here -> checkboxes seeded from live.option_ids
- Seal -> plan.choose -> invalidation refetches plan.current -> sealed block renders from the daemon's answer

## Expected impact
The operator can no longer overwrite the live plan by accident after a reload, sees which report the live plan came from, and sees what a re-seal would change before paying for a multi-second LLM call. One source of truth for the plan across Reconcile and On-air.

## Evaluation
Claim: the composer reflects the daemon's live plan, not a volatile copy.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (planState.ts does not exist; with a fresh session the plan page renders no sealed block and offers 'Seal this plan' over nothing).
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first (planState.test.ts table + layer2.test.tsx mounts with a scripted plan.current)
Result: better
Gate: architecture
evidence: session.ts:20 `readonly sealed: Readonly<Record<string, NextStreamPlan>>;` | PlanPage.tsx:46 `sealed={s.sealed[reportId]}` | PlanPage.tsx:99 `Nothing chosen yet: the plan rides on the directives alone` | rpc.rs:257 `"plan.current" => match state.reconciler.next_plan()? {` | lib.rs:560 `write_json_atomic(&self.cfg.data_dir.join("next_plan.json"), &plan)?;` | grep -rn 'plan\.current' apps/console/src (non-test): data/invalidation.ts:16, pages/onair/Dispatch.tsx:58, pages/onair/Layer1.tsx:120 - none in pages/reconcile

critic.reason: Grounded, falsifiable single-authority fix for a real accidental-overwrite path.

body:
## Summary
The operator keeps, drops and deactivates standing directives blind. Every reconcile report already carries a computed outcome per directive - held, broken, attempted, ignored or unmeasured, with n, a 95% bound and transcript refs - and the console renders none of it. Put the verdict beside each directive and in the report, so Deactivate and Keep are decided against evidence.

## Description
WP15 made the reconciler judge the Lord's directives (lib.rs:317-319, summary.rs:126-131) and ship them as `ReconcileReport.directives` (types.ts:2485-2488). A zero-consumer grep over apps/console finds no reader. The Directives tab (DirectivesPage.tsx:154-160) lists kind/text/scope/added/state; the Report tab (ReportPage.tsx:59-67) skips the field. The only trace is a sentence the daemon appends to the prose summary (lib.rs:320-323).

The change leans on hitl-approval `oracle-before-gate` (show the decider what to judge the item against) and measurement-honesty `minimum-sample-floors` (a rate never without its n, small samples marked). `model.ts` gains `outcomeIndex` and `outcomeOrder`; a new `DirectiveOutcomes.tsx` renders a verdict cell (chip + 'held k of n' + bound via RateBar + RefLinks into Brain transcripts) and a report section. DirectivesPage reads the report on show through the existing `useReportId`/`useReport` hooks, adds an Outcome column and a Broken facet beside Active/Proposed/All/Off, and names which report the verdicts come from. ReportPage adds 'The Lord's directives' worst-first, naming each by its directive.list text. A missing outcome reads 'Not judged', never 'Held'.

## Flow
- Open Directives -> directive.list + report on show (already cached by the poster)
- Each row: verdict chip, rate with n and bound, refs -> Brain transcript line
- Facet Broken -> only directives the character broke -> Deactivate in place
- Report tab -> directives section worst-first, beside segments and incidents

## Expected impact
The directive loop closes in the console: the operator sees which standing orders the character obeys, which it breaks and where, and which no run measured, and prunes them with one click instead of reading transcripts to guess.

## Evaluation
Claim: every directive's judged outcome is visible where the operator decides on it.
Before: 0 of 7 acceptance cases pass (no outcomeIndex; no outcome column, facet or report section).
After: 7 of 7
Method: gate - acceptance tests written first (model.test.ts + layer2.test.tsx with genReport carrying directives)
Result: better
Gate: none (read-only render of a field already on the wire)
